props.title: The Devil's Miner

sections.content: The Devil's Miner stands among the most haunting documentaries about child labor, following 14-year-old Basilio Vargas and his younger brother as they work in Bolivia's notorious Cerro Rico silver mines. Directors Kief Davidson and Richard Ladkani capture the brutal reality of children who must venture into the treacherous mines of Potosí, where miners worship "El Tio" (the devil) for protection. This documentary connects directly to other powerful films about child labor and exploitation in Latin America, like Los Olvidados (1950) by Luis Buñuel and Pixote (1981) by Hector Babenco.

sections.content: The film's exploration of indigenous spiritual beliefs merged with Catholic traditions echoes through other significant Latin American documentaries. Nostalgia for the Light (2010) similarly examines Chile's Atacama Desert, connecting astronomical observation with the search for remains of political disappearances. Like The Devil's Miner, it weaves together landscape, history, and human struggle. The tradition of observational mining documentaries extends to Frederick Wiseman's Presque Isle (1991) and Johan van der Keuken's The Eye Above the Well (1988).

Davidson and Ladkani's intimate cinematography inside the mines creates claustrophobic tension reminiscent of fiction films like The 33 (2015) and Coal Miner's Daughter (1980). However, their documentary approach avoids melodrama, instead letting the harsh reality of child miners speak for itself. The film's examination of economic exploitation connects to later works like Darwin's Nightmare (2004) and Workingman's Death (2005). SUBHEAD: Child Labor Documentation in Cinema

sections.content: The Devil's Miner belongs to a crucial lineage of films exposing child labor, including Born into Brothels (2004) and Children Underground (2001). These documentaries share an approach that balances journalistic exposure with deep empathy for their subjects. The film's portrayal of Basilio's determination to continue his education despite working in the mines particularly resonates with On the Way to School (2013) and Promises (2001).
